title: Machine learning builds EsoralPrint, a transcriptomic score for oral and esophageal cancer
summary: Using 2,541 samples, 34 intrasample ordinal gene pairs were engineered into a single-sample score trained on oral tissue and externally validated across cohorts, technical platforms and tissue sites. The score separated low-risk hyperplasia that progressed to cancer. Numerical performance values are not given here.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine learning with 34 intrasample ordinal gene pairs (EsoralPrint)
organization: University of Nebraska Medical Center; Aiphaqua Clinomics

evidence.tested: Generalisation of a transcriptomic score across external oral and esophageal cohorts and platforms.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective transcriptomic cohorts; abstract numbers incomplete; clinical use not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Interpretable machine learning deriving gene-pair features for a malignancy score.
